inventory_method: All 70 resource entries in the public index page's serialized pagination data, cross-checked against canonical URLs in Temporal's public sitemap. Logos and unrelated resource-library entries are excluded.
evidence_policy: Observations paraphrase published text. Transferable lessons are engineering inferences, not claims of customer implementation. Video summaries are not full transcripts or watched videos; inaccessible transcripts remain an explicit limitation.

stories.title: How Jota runs banking and AI workflows on Temporal
stories.evidence_note: Read the full published case-study text and verified the canonical page; no video was required.
stories.observed_pattern: Jota separates conversation orchestration from banking operations and returns actual operation results to the agent. It persists waits for customer confirmation and correlates conversations with banking execution.
stories.transferable_lesson: Inference: bind each requested tool action to a durable operation and feed its confirmed or explicitly unknown outcome back to the model. Preserve approval identity across retries and waits.
stories.bug_to_prevent: The assistant announces a transfer succeeded before the banking operation completes, or a repeated confirmation creates another transfer.
stories.limitations: The story does not establish exactly-once external effects. Its recommendation to use local Activities for database access is workload-specific, not a universal rule. Worker-versioning adoption is described as future work.

stories.title: How Strada built durable AI insurance agents with Temporal
stories.evidence_note: Read the full published case-study text. The web reader failed for this URL; an independent HTTP request returned 200 and confirmed the expected article content.
stories.observed_pattern: Strada isolates attachment processing, bounds its reasoning loop, persists responses before delivery, and serializes reasoning over overlapping customer context. Activities have different retry policies by failure class; its long-lived coordinator uses Continue-As-New.
stories.transferable_lesson: Inference: choose failure boundaries deliberately, serialize only the shared decision scope, and carry pending work across history rollover. Durable delivery records still need a retry-safe send protocol.
stories.bug_to_prevent: Concurrent agents issue contradictory replies; one failed attachment restarts successful work; coordinator rollover loses queued requests; a retried send duplicates email.
stories.limitations: No implementation or replay histories are supplied. Persist-before-send alone cannot prove duplicate-free delivery, and serial orchestration can become a throughput bottleneck.

stories.title: Scaling AI-powered education with durable workflows
stories.evidence_note: Read the full published case-study text and verified the canonical page; architecture diagrams were not needed for these textual observations.
stories.observed_pattern: Maria Educação uses domain pipelines with per-step Activities, child-workflow fan-out, concurrency caps, dedicated workers for heavy processing, and heartbeats for external job polling. Some agent reasoning is a LangGraph graph inside one Activity.
stories.transferable_lesson: Inference: align durable checkpoints with costly retry boundaries, cap aggregate provider demand, and separate resource-heavy work. Identify which inner graph steps lack their own durable checkpoint.
stories.bug_to_prevent: Retrying one graph Activity unexpectedly repeats successful model calls, unbounded fan-out exhausts provider quotas, or missing heartbeats delay recovery from a dead polling worker.
stories.limitations: The narrative alternates between one Activity per model call and whole graphs inside Activities. Its no-repeat claims do not address completion-recording failures or internal graph checkpoint semantics.

stories.title: How ShareChat rebuilt subscription billing on Temporal and reached 99.9% reliability
stories.evidence_note: Read the full published case-study text and verified the canonical page; regulatory claims are treated as historical customer context, not current legal guidance.
stories.observed_pattern: ShareChat replaced independently scheduled notification and collection jobs with ordered billing-cycle workflows. A cycle captures configuration once, uses durable timing and retry limits, and supports versioned evolution. Migration proceeded by product with metric checks.
stories.transferable_lesson: Inference: encode prerequisite confirmation and deadlines explicitly; snapshot business configuration per logical cycle; evolve active runs compatibly and migrate with measurable rollback criteria.
stories.bug_to_prevent: A collection runs before its notification is confirmed, live configuration alters an active cycle, or old and new schedulers both bill a subscription.
stories.limitations: Do not copy the story's regulatory timing or retry numbers without current verification. Infinite notification retries and recursively created cycles require explicit cancellation, lifetime, and history bounds.

stories.title: How SMILe uses Temporal to orchestrate multi-channel logistics Workflows
stories.evidence_note: Read the full published case-study text and verified the canonical page.
stories.observed_pattern: SMILe models booking lifecycles as workflows, keeps routing and sequencing in orchestration, and places partner integrations in Activities. Asynchronous partner updates influence the ongoing process.
stories.transferable_lesson: Inference: record routing inputs through replay-safe boundaries and correlate each external update to the correct booking and operation. Give integration failures their own recovery policy.
stories.bug_to_prevent: Replay reads fresh partner availability and chooses a different route, or an old delivery event mutates the wrong booking state.
stories.limitations: The story gives no concrete event-ordering, deduplication, or provider-idempotency mechanism. Durable workflow state alone does not make integrations safe.

stories.title: Mews: Hospitality, payments, and durability on a global scale
stories.evidence_note: Read the full published case-study text and verified the canonical page.
stories.observed_pattern: Mews extracted variable-duration bill closing into an independent workflow, models refund settlement waits with a cutoff, and coordinates dispute and onboarding events with Signals. It reports using patching and replay tests when changing webhook workflows.
stories.transferable_lesson: Inference: isolate variable-duration work when the business dependency permits it, make retry eligibility and deadlines explicit, and replay representative active histories before rollout.
stories.bug_to_prevent: A slow operation blocks unrelated payment work, a settlement-dependent refund retries forever, or changed command ordering breaks in-flight executions.
stories.limitations: Outage recovery is customer-reported. The article does not specify payment idempotency or patch-retirement rules; replay tests alone cannot validate all external side effects.

stories.title: How Emergent runs 1 billion+ agent Actions per month on Temporal Cloud
stories.evidence_note: Read the full published case-study text and verified the canonical page.
stories.observed_pattern: Emergent's agent originally shared the resource-constrained execution sandbox and died with it. Its Temporal design separates orchestration, uses child workflows for agent coordination, supports human waits, and checks workflow changes through replay.
stories.transferable_lesson: Inference: keep orchestration alive independently of disposable tool environments; persist sandbox identity and reconcile its state after failure. Specify child cancellation, termination, and cleanup behavior rather than assuming inheritance is sufficient.
stories.bug_to_prevent: A tool-induced memory failure kills its own recovery controller, retries leak sandboxes, or cancellation leaves child work running.
stories.limitations: Child workflows provide logical execution boundaries, not automatic process or resource isolation. The case study's availability language does not establish universal downtime guarantees.

stories.title: How Nooks scaled their AI platform 100x without breaking
stories.evidence_note: Read the full published case-study text and verified the canonical page.

stories.transferable_lesson: Inference: select overlap behavior from freshness and completeness requirements, bound accumulated work, and track synchronization checkpoints. Limit provider-wide concurrency across chunks and retries.
stories.bug_to_prevent: Slow recurring syncs create an ever-growing backlog, overlapping runs overwrite newer data, or independently capped workers collectively exceed provider quotas.
stories.limitations: BUFFER_ALL is a customer choice, not a universal recommendation. The article does not specify deduplication, consistency, or aggregate rate-limiting algorithms.

stories.title: How Retool built robust Workflow and Agents products on Temporal
stories.evidence_note: Read the full written case study and verified its canonical page. The embedded interview was not watched or transcribed; conclusions use only the article.

stories.transferable_lesson: Inference: define one durable lifecycle for an agent task and reuse established orchestration primitives, while specifying tool-call boundaries, stopping conditions, and ownership of human input.
stories.bug_to_prevent: An agent loses task state while waiting, or an unbounded reasoning loop continues calling tools without reaching a terminal or escalated outcome.
stories.limitations: This is a high-level product case study with no code, retry contracts, or concrete failure analysis. Boundaries and safeguards in the lesson are engineering inferences.

stories.title: How VEED.IO powers four million daily video workflows with Temporal

stories.transferable_lesson: Inference: centralize provider adapters with explicit retry, timeout, error, and cost contracts. Count attempts and externally billed operations separately, and adopt the model incrementally with representative failures.
stories.bug_to_prevent: Repeated provider requests silently multiply cost, different workflows classify the same provider error inconsistently, or a broad migration spreads an untested adapter defect.
stories.limitations: A workflow Activity count is not necessarily the number of externally billed calls. The story supplies no provider idempotency guarantees or cost-reconciliation implementation.

stories.title: FireHydrant: Durable alerting and faster incident response with Temporal
stories.evidence_note: Read the full published case-study text and verified the canonical page; outage claims were not independently audited.

stories.transferable_lesson: Inference: correlate executions to business incidents, persist the transition that makes an action newly eligible, and explicitly test duplicate events and schema compatibility across workers.
stories.bug_to_prevent: A burst triggers the same escalation repeatedly, a late acknowledgment fails to stop escalation, or incompatible payloads fail after a deployment.
stories.limitations: The article does not show the send-deduplication or rule-transition implementation. Its outage experience cannot guarantee notification delivery during arbitrary dependency failures.

stories.title: Duolingo simplifies self-service infrastructure with Temporal Nexus
stories.evidence_note: Read the full published case-study text and verified the canonical page. The page contains inconsistent wording about the current Slack approval interface.
stories.observed_pattern: Duolingo exposes selected infrastructure operations through Nexus across team-owned Namespaces. A portal and gateway initiate workflows; sensitive operations retain approval steps, and workers have narrowly scoped infrastructure permissions.
stories.transferable_lesson: Inference: expose a small operation contract across ownership boundaries and enforce authorization, approval identity, and resource permissions independently. Preserve status visibility without granting callers general administrative control.
stories.bug_to_prevent: Self-service callers gain broad Namespace access, replayed approvals authorize different parameters, or a worker role can perform unrelated destructive operations.
stories.limitations: Nexus does not replace application authorization or cloud IAM. The closing section places Slack approvals in future plans, while earlier prose suggests they already exist. Verify current SDK support separately.

stories.title: Replit uses Temporal to power Replit Agent reliably at scale
stories.evidence_note: Read the complete published case-study text and verified the live Temporal page.
stories.observed_pattern: Replit describes a Workflow per agent session, Activities for nondeterministic execution, and Updates for user interactions including consent. It also orchestrates deployments and domain lifecycles.
stories.transferable_lesson: Inference: Give each session a stable business identity and define conflict/reuse behavior. Persist consent in orchestration state, and make external process creation and tools safe under repeated Activity attempts.
stories.bug_to_prevent: Duplicate agent processes or repeated external actions despite having only one active Workflow ID.
stories.limitations: A unique running Workflow is not proof that an external agent process or Activity runs exactly once. The case study does not expose fencing, process reconciliation, or idempotency implementation. Reported availability is customer-specific.

stories.title: Lindy boosts reliability and observability of AI agents with Temporal Cloud
stories.evidence_note: Read the complete published case-study text and verified the live Temporal page.
stories.observed_pattern: Lindy reports replacing queue-based orchestration that lost visibility around API failures and pod shutdowns with durable, observable agent execution spanning model calls and integrations.
stories.transferable_lesson: Inference: Make progress and failure states inspectable across worker replacement; place nondeterministic integrations behind Activity boundaries and distinguish transient retryable failures from terminal outcomes.
stories.bug_to_prevent: An automation silently stops after a worker exits or an external API times out, leaving neither recovery nor an actionable operational signal.
stories.limitations: The short article uses broad Workflow terminology for wake-ups and individual calls; it provides no code or precise boundary model. Do not interpret it as permission for direct network calls inside Workflow code or evidence of universal queue-system inadequacy.

stories.title: Attentive migrates to Temporal Cloud for infrastructure cost savings and increased application reliability
stories.evidence_note: Read the complete published case-study text and verified the live Temporal page.
stories.observed_pattern: Attentive describes persistence compatibility and scaling problems while self-hosting, progressive namespace migration through development, staging, and production, and discovery of ongoing Workflows belonging to an inactive customer.
stories.transferable_lesson: Inference: Test migration against active executions and Schedules, audit lifecycle ownership, and monitor work whose business owner has disappeared. Evaluate hosting against actual storage, upgrade, and operational constraints.
stories.bug_to_prevent: Abandoned recurring work keeps executing, or a migration loses in-flight state and scheduled work.
stories.limitations: The migration service was prerelease and vendor-assisted in this account; verify current support and procedures. Their choice to terminate stale Workflows is not a general recommendation to bypass cancellation or business cleanup. Cost conclusions are workload-specific.

stories.title: Gradient Labs uses AI agents to resolve complex customer issues in financial services
stories.evidence_note: Read the complete published case-study text and verified the live Temporal page.
stories.observed_pattern: Gradient Labs identifies successful model requests with unusable outputs as a distinct failure mode. Its conversation Workflows retain state across long interactions and use timers for follow-up.
stories.transferable_lesson: Inference: Validate model outputs explicitly; classify invalid results and bound regeneration separately from network retries. Retry the failed step without redoing prior confirmed external actions, and measure semantic quality independently of execution completion.
stories.bug_to_prevent: Invalid model output is treated as success, or unlimited regeneration repeatedly spends money and duplicates an earlier tool effect.
stories.limitations: The article implies bad model outputs automatically cause errors and retries. Temporal does not supply domain-specific output validation; application code and SDK failure configuration must establish that behavior. No retry budget or concrete validator is published.

stories.title: How Vinted Runs 10 to 12 Million Workflows a Day with Temporal While Keeping Dev Velocity High and Costs Low
stories.evidence_note: Read the complete published case-study text and verified the live Temporal page.
stories.observed_pattern: Vinted began with a limited background flow and controlled adoption with feature flags. It encountered oversized payloads, unintended Ruby return values, and serialization problems, and added queue-oriented metrics beyond CPU and memory.
stories.transferable_lesson: Inference: Stage adoption with a single execution owner per business operation; review serialized inputs and results, use references for bulky data, and observe schedule-to-start latency and queue pressure.
stories.bug_to_prevent: An implicit return serializes an unexpectedly large object, or workers appear healthy while tasks accumulate unprocessed.
stories.limitations: The case study's broad locking and retry claims do not specify external-effect safety. Parallel legacy and Temporal paths need ownership controls absent from the article. Self-hosting economics and workload scale are not portable guarantees.

stories.title: Gorgias uses AI agents to help over 15,000 e-commerce brands improve customer service
stories.evidence_note: Read the complete published case-study text and verified the live Temporal page.
stories.observed_pattern: Gorgias moved from answering questions to agents that perform order operations. Its requirements included external API retries, compensation across steps, asynchronous results, and durable pauses; support, sales, and synthesis agents have distinct Workflows.
stories.transferable_lesson: Inference: Treat action-taking agents as distributed business processes. Define each effect's authorization, idempotency, failure classification, and compensation before composing agents; use durable waits for external or human responses.
stories.bug_to_prevent: A retried return or cancellation duplicates an external effect, or partial completion is concealed behind a successful chat response.
stories.limitations: No saga implementation, transaction guarantee, or compensation policy is supplied. The article's suggestion that retry complexities disappear must not replace application-level retry and side-effect design.

stories.title: How Trendyol’s Database Team Scales for 200K Merchants and 1M+ Orders a Day
stories.evidence_note: Read the complete published case-study text and verified the live Temporal page.
stories.observed_pattern: Trendyol describes a parent Workflow starting regional database-creation child Workflows in parallel. Children check provisioning readiness through Activities separated by durable waits; replication starts after both regions are ready.
stories.transferable_lesson: Inference: Model dependency joins explicitly and distinguish submitted provisioning from confirmed readiness. Make resource creation repeat-safe, use durable waiting, and add deadlines, cancellation, and history-growth management for prolonged polling.
stories.bug_to_prevent: Replication starts before prerequisites exist, or a retry creates duplicate infrastructure after an uncertain provisioning response.
stories.limitations: The article does not establish resource idempotency or database consistency guarantees. Its generic sleep notation should not be copied as SDK-specific code. Readiness polling needs a workload-appropriate choice between timers, retried checks, heartbeats, and external notifications.

stories.title: How Vodafone aims to orchestrate value added services across devices with Temporal
stories.evidence_note: Read the complete published case-study text and verified the live Temporal page.
stories.observed_pattern: Vodafone separates device-control domains and campaign orchestration across Namespaces. It distinguishes steady onboarding traffic from fleet-wide update bursts and retains responsibility for worker scaling when adopting Temporal Cloud.
stories.transferable_lesson: Inference: Isolate competing workloads intentionally, bound campaign fan-out, and size workers and downstream rate limits independently of service capacity. Define ownership when old and new device controllers coexist.
stories.bug_to_prevent: A fleet campaign starves onboarding, overwhelms device APIs, or races another controller into conflicting updates.
stories.limitations: Namespace layout alone does not prove resource isolation or prevent external split brain. Payload confidentiality requires a configured client-side codec; metadata remains a separate concern. Cloud scaling and hosting-cost comparisons do not remove worker capacity planning.

stories.title: Mollie Payments maximizes operational efficiency using Temporal
stories.evidence_note: Read the complete published case-study text and verified the live Temporal page.

stories.transferable_lesson: Inference: Adopt orchestration where waiting, coordination, or recovery justify it; preserve a simpler design otherwise. Connect invitation cadence to actual downstream capacity and verify which payloads and metadata can expose personal information.
stories.bug_to_prevent: Missing invitations silently leave downstream staff idle, or personal data leaks through unprotected metadata despite encrypted payloads.
stories.limitations: The account does not publish its encryption configuration or workload-balancing algorithm. Durable execution supports process recovery but does not itself establish regulatory compliance, data minimization, or correct capacity allocation.
